First, we start with setting up the matrices for the various units and the global production. In this case, each unit has a Product Unit value and the Primary Product Units. This is a 12x3 matrix, I named it as 'original_matrix'.  next, we create a matrix for 'primary_product_units' based on the num_partitions_in_units and add zeros in the order of the primary_product_as_string. This is a 100x3 matrix. We name this matrix as 'modified_matrix'. Lastly, we multiply the 'original_matrix' and the 770x3 matrix as 'target_matrix'. This is our final matrix. The formulae are below:
target_matrix = original_matrix * modified_matrix
Next, we can check matrix norms.
print(f"Original matrix norm is {original_matrix.norm(1):.6f}.")
print(f"Modified matrix norm is {modified_matrix.norm(1):.6f}.")
print(f"Target matrix norm is {target_matrix.norm(1):.6f}.")

The second one said that when it was under the light, the vegetable turned bright, while the first one claimed that it was a true green. While trying the same vegetable at home, as soon as the family went out due to work, nothing changed. This did not set the friends up well, and the first one demanded that the green vegetable be sold.
